text:
Maya (PM): quick sync — we need to pick one major inference perf initiative for the next sprint. options:
1) Hotpath latency work (p95 -20%): prefetch + hot KV cache + priority routing. targets enterprise SLOs.
2) Throughput uplift for batch-heavy customers: smarter batching, async workers, higher parallelism to drop $/token.
3) Quantization rollout (int8/4bit profiles): material cost wins but risk of quality regressions and eval + infra changes.

Which should be the sprint bet? pls share RICE-ish numbers (rough) and launch criteria. i want a 1-sentence recommendation + main risk.

Leo (Eng): i lean latency hotpath. impact medium-high for product features, confidence high on infra work (we've prototyped prefetch). effort estimate: 3 engineers x 2 weeks (sprint).
R: reach = % of requests on hotpath ~40%
I: estimated retention / revenue uplift = medium (increases conversion for low-latency customers)
C: 0.7
E: effort = 6 eng-weeks
score ~ (40*??*0.7)/6 if we used simple math.
Main risk: cache invalidation complexity + lock contention at scale.

Priya (SRE): agree latency is high-value for SLOs. ops caveat: prefetch changes alter traffic shape -> watch memory + KV eviction. rollout needs canary by tenant and a fallback to current routing. also we need tracing hooks to verify cache hit ratios. effort includes telemetry work.

Carlos (Data): numbers from last quarter: 42% of requests are interactive low-latency, 33% batch_embed/async, top 5 customers = 58% token consumption. if we only optimize throughput, top customers see the biggest $/token drop. ballpark: throughput uplift could reduce cost for heavy customers by 15-20% (for them) which affects renewals.

Sam (Eng Platform): throughput work is broader — requires changes to serving runtime batching & queueing heuristics. effort likely heavier (8-10 eng-weeks) but reusable. risk is longer lead time. quantization needs model-team + eval harness; not infra-first.

Maya (PM): ok helpful. quick RICE stabs from above:
- Latency: Reach 40, Impact medium-high, Confidence 0.7, Effort 6 -> favors latency for customer-facing SLOs.
- Throughput: Reach 33, Impact high for big customers, Confidence 0.6, Effort 9 -> high ROI for a subset but longer.
- Quant: Reach variable, Impact cost-low, Confidence 0.5, Effort 5 (because evals take time) -> carries quality risk.

Maya (PM): recommendation: pick latency hotpath as primary sprint objective + start a small parallel spike for throughput (1 engineer) and a blocked ticket for quant evals. launch criteria for latency: p95 reduced by >=15% on canary tenants, cache hit ratio > X (TBD), no increase in error rate or tail mem OOMs.

Leo (Eng): +1. concrete deliverables:
- prefetch + cache: impl + canary route config (by tenant)
- tracing/counters: hit ratio, eviction rate, request latency histograms
- fallback path: toggle to drain prefetch on failure

Priya (SRE): i'll draft the canary plan and required dashboards. need a rollback runbook and perf budget alert (memory and CPU).

Carlos (Data): i'll produce a 48h dashboard comparing canary tenants vs baseline and a small cohort analysis for top customers.

Sam (Eng Platform): i'll scope the throughput spike: one engineer 2 sprints to prototype improved batching strategy and a perf harness. if promising we schedule full work in next cycle.

Maya (PM): vote with emoji: :one: latency primary, :two: throughput primary, :three: quant primary. i'll take final call tomorrow EOD.

Leo (Eng): :one:
Priya (SRE): :one:
Carlos (Data): :two: (but :one: if governance wants faster customer SLO wins)
Sam (Eng Platform): :one: (and will start spike)

Maya (PM): thanks. added tickets to the sprint board and linked RICE comments. will post final decision after talking to sales about top customer deadlines.

deploy-bot: scheduled maintenance window 1958769000-1958772600 (heads-up if we need deploys during that time)

Maya (PM): noted — we'll avoid canary cutovers during that window.

Leo (Eng): ok, starting branches for prefetch + metrics. will ping when ready for review.
